summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun
details: @servicetitan/microfront-auth@0.0.8 declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ at install time, extracts it, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a ~728 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob (hex-mangled identifiers, numeric opcode table, rotating string-array decoder — obfuscator.io-style loader), and `setup.mjs` itself is string-array obfuscated. Fetching an alternate language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated in-tarball payload at `npm install` bypasses Node-based tooling and hides the payload from static inspection; this is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern, not a legitimate use of Bun. The package publishes under the `@servicetitan` scope with an empty description and a `servicetitan/playground` repo, consistent with namespace impersonation of the ServiceTitan brand.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
